national_raw_news.title: UPI stays free for users, vast majority of transactions to remain free for merchants as well, says government
national_raw_news.content: Updated - August 09, 2026 12:40 pm IST - New Delhi BENGALURU KARNATAKA 19/07/25 : Amid taxes on UPI transactions for small traders and street vendors continue to use digital form of UPI payments, after commercial taxes issued them notices in Bengaluru on July 19, 2025. PHOTO : ALLEN EGENUSE J / The Hindu | Photo Credit: J. Allen Egenuse The government sought to shut down speculation on plans to impose fees on the country's ubiquitous digital payments network, saying on Saturday (August 8, 2026) that consumers will not have to pay transaction charges for using UPI, while the vast majority of merchant transactions will also remain free. The government said any future merchant discount rate (MDR), if introduced, would apply only to a limited set of merchant transactions above a specified threshold and at a nominal rate, which would be lower than typical debit and credit card MDRs. Paywall: On a charge on UPI transactions All person-to-person UPI transactions will continue to be free, it said. The clarification comes after an amendment to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, sparked a debate over whether the government was preparing to impose charges on UPI transactions. The proposed change to Section 10A of the law is an "enabling provision" and does not itself impose an MDR, the government said in a statement. If Parliament passes the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, the UPI and Services Steering Committee headed by the National Payments Corp. of India (NPCI) will decide on the MDR, if any, according to the government. The government said any future MDR would be threshold-based rather than imposed across all UPI transactions, with the "vast majority" of merchant payments continuing to be free. The proposed framework is aimed at creating a more sustainable revenue model for UPI as transaction volumes surge and the system requires continued investment in cybersecurity, fraud prevention and payment infrastructure, it said. United Payment Interface, or UPI, has become the world's largest real-time payment system since its launch in 2016-17, processing 2,366 crore transactions worth ₹29.9 lakh crore in July 2026 alone. The platform is now live in 11 foreign countries, with several others expressing interest in adopting or integrating UPI, the government said. The statement comes two days after the Lok Sabha passed a Bill to amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, which authorises the government to permit banks and other service providers to levy charges on payments through UPI and other notified electronic payment modes. "Once the Parliament passes the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which proposes to amend Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the 'UPI and Services Steering Committee' headed by NPCI will decide on the MDR, if any," it said. The recent amendment to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act (PSS Act) has generated a debate, with some misinterpreting it as a move to impose charges on ordinary users, it said, adding, in reality, the amendment is an enabling provision designed to ensure UPI's long-term sustainability, technological advancement, and resilience against emerging risks. ALSO WATCH Watch: UPI charges: Will users have to pay in the future? | Above the Fold | 07.08.2026 Explaining the rationale, the statement said that with exponential transaction volumes, the system requires significant and continuous upgrades in cybersecurity, fraud prevention, and infrastructure. The statement further said that it was required for market expansion and self-sustainability. It is necessary to increase competition by encouraging more companies to expand their operations, which requires a self-sustaining revenue model, it said. Reliance on subsidies alone is not viable for the next wave of growth, it said, adding that a balanced framework is required to ensure that UPI remains robust, inclusive, and future-ready. Addressing concerns on narratives like external influences may be driving policy changes, the statement said, this is unfounded, completely false and misleading. If external pressure had been a factor, the government would not have introduced UPI in 2016 or made it free of charge for both merchants as well as citizens since January 2020 and ensured that it became the world's largest real-time interoperable payment system, it said. The amendment should therefore be viewed in the context of the government's broader objective of ensuring that India's digital payment infrastructure remains sustainable, competitive, innovative and capable of serving the country's rapidly expanding digital economy, it said. UPI is India's own innovation, and the government remains committed to keeping it free for citizens while ensuring its sustainability for decades to come, it added. India now stands at the cusp of the next wave of digital payments growth, it said, adding that to expand UPI further into rural and semi-urban areas and maintain competitiveness, the UPI ecosystem must be self — sustainable and affordable. The amendment to the PSS Act is a forward-looking step to ensure that UPI continues to thrive as a secure, affordable, inclusive, and globally recognised payment system, it said. Since its launch in 2016-17, the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has transformed India's digital economy into one of the most inclusive and dynamic payment ecosystems in the world, it said. What began as a bold experiment in real-time, interoperable payments has now become a global benchmark, processing billions of transactions every month and reaching deep into the fabric of everyday life, it said. Today, it said, UPI has grown into the world's largest real-time payment system, processing 2,366 crore transactions worth ₹29.9 lakh crore in July 2026 alone. UPI is now also live in 11 foreign countries, and many other countries have shown interest. UPI is a national achievement built by Indians, for Indians. The government has promoted, funded and grown it for a decade, and will continue to do so. Citizens are requested to rely only on official information from the Ministry of Finance, the Reserve Bank of India and NPCI, and not to forward unverified messages, it added. national_raw_news.title: Punjab CM writes to Governor favouring parole for convict in Beant Singh’s assassination case
national_raw_news.content: Updated - August 09, 2026 12:39 pm IST - Chandigarh Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann. File photo: @AAPPunjab X via ANI Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Saturday (August 8, 2026) wrote to Governor Gulab Chand Kataria favouring the grant of 10-day parole to Jagtar Singh Hawara, jailed for life for the assassination of then Chief Minister Beant Singh in 1995, to enable him to meet his ailing mother. Last month, the Punjab and Haryana High Court directed authorities in Delhi's Mandoli prison, where Hawara is lodged, to decide the parole application of the Babbar Khalsa terrorist in a time-bound manner after seeking recommendations of the Chandigarh Administration. In his letter to the Governor, who is also Chandigarh Administrator, Mr. Mann said, "Owing to her old age, the mother of Jagtar Singh Hawara is facing age-related health issues. This has resulted in deterioration of her health, which is a major cause of concern for everyone." Appealing for relief on humanitarian grounds, Mr. Mann said, "Jagtar Singh Hawara has also filed CRWP No. 3868/2026 before the Punjab and Haryana High Court, Chandigarh, seeking directions for his release on parole." He further said, "The High Court has also directed that his parole application be considered." Mr. Mann requested the Punjab Governor to consider granting 10 days' parole to Hawara at the earliest on humanitarian grounds. "It is imperative because of the deteriorating health condition of his mother," he said. Over a week back, a delegation of Shiromani Akali Dal (Punar Surjit) had met the Punjab Governor here and sought his intervention in allowing Hawara to meet his ailing mother. Hawara was sentenced to death, but it was commuted by the High Court. He is serving imprisonment for the rest of his life in the case related to the blast at the entrance of the civil secretariat at Chandigarh on August 31, 1995, in which Beant Singh and 16 more people were killed. national_raw_news.title: Vande Mataram row: Kerala’s UDF govt. again faces allegations of toeing the RSS line
national_raw_news.content: Published - August 09, 2026 12:36 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM The directive signed by Chief Secretary Bishwanath Sinha (right) on August 6 asked government departments to ensure the recital of Vande Mataram in its entirety during the Independence Day celebrations, as per the Union government’s instructions. File | Photo Credit: Nirmal Harindran The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Kerala has yet again found itself at the centre of allegations over toeing the Sangh Parivar’s line after the Chief Secretary’s recent directive asking government departments to ensure the recital of Vande Mataram in its entirety during the Independence Day celebrations, as per the Union government’s instructions. Even as the Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) lashed out at the UDF government for “surrendering completely” to the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)’s agenda, the Ministers of the ruling front — including those from the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) — found it hard to defend the order. The Chief Minister’s office is yet to make an official reaction. The Vande Mataram controversy is the latest in a series of decisions of the UDF government, which have been criticised for following a pro-Sangh Parivar line. As per the directive signed by Chief Secretary Bishwanath Sinha on August 6, the Union Ministry of Culture had on July 14 communicated that the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign will be observed this year from August 9 to 17. The campaign has been integrated with the third phase of the nationwide commemoration of the 150 years of Vande Mataram. Accordingly, all physical celebrations during this period have to combine the collective singing of Vande Mataram with the hoisting of the National Flag. The letter further says that the “instructions of the Government of India for recitation of Vande Mataram will be followed in full”. The Local Self Government department and the General Education Department are the nodal departments for the programme. However, an earlier circular issued by the General Administration Department on August 4 does not make any mention of Vande Mataram recital as part of Independence Day celebrations. In February this year, the Union government had made it mandatory to play or sing the full song at all government events. On July 30, the Parliament passed amid the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, making intentional insult to Vande Mataram a punishable offence. Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan said that singing the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram was not wrong, but the song in its entirety goes against the secular spirit of the country. The later stanzas of the song refer to deities of a specific religion. “The Constituent Assembly and leaders like Jawaharlal Nehru was of the opinion that only the first two stanzas need to be sung. This has remained so until the swearing in of the current UDF government when it was sung in full. Despite the widespread criticism against that, the government has now issued such an order. The UDF government has completely surrendered itself to the RSS agenda,” Mr. Vijayan alleged. CPI(M) Central Committee member T.M. Thomas Isaac said that even though in a federal system States might sometimes be forced to follow central directives, the State should at least make a mark of protest. CPI(M) State Secretary M.V.Govindan said that the latest order promulgated has further reinforced the public perception that the UDF government has mutated into an ideological proxy for the Hindutva agenda-driven Union government. He said that the Constituent Assembly had concluded that the final four stanzas of Vande Mataram had a pronouncedly Hindu-majoritarian tint that could potentially undermine national unity and should be best avoided. He also accused the IUML of supplicantly falling in line with the UDF government’s soft-hindutva political line without the whimper of a protest. Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala said that he was unaware of the directive, while Health Minister K. Muraleedharan said that only two stanzas of Vande Mataram will be sung in the State government’s events. IUML leaders appeared to take divergent stands on the issue. Education Minister N. Shamsudheen claimed that the State government had nothing to with the directive. The Chief Secretary had to issue such a directive as per directions from the Lok Bhavan. Industries Minister P.K. Kunhalikutty said that the IUML has never sung Vande Mataram in full. “Our policy is similar to the stand taken by the Congress at the national level. I will speak about the legal aspects of this after speaking to the CM,” he said. Published - August 09, 2026 12:36 pm IST Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. national_raw_news.title: Dravidian movement played a key role in temple entry struggles: Kanimozhi
national_raw_news.content: Updated - August 09, 2026 12:28 pm IST - CHENNAI MP K. Kanimozhi, Justice N. Anand Venkatesh, senior advocate Ramani Natarajan, and advocate and author of The People’s Sanctum Manuraj Shunmugasundaram at the event held to launch the book in Chennai on Saturday. | Photo Credit: J. Johan Sathyadas DMK MP K. Kanimozhi said on Saturday that the Dravidian movement, which believed that a religion preserving caste ought to be dismantled, was the very movement that fought continuously and successfully to ensure no barriers existed for believers who wished to enter temples. She made these remarks at the book release event for The People’s Sanctum , authored by advocate Manuraj Shunmugasundaram, held at the Victoria Public Hall in Chennai. Ms. Kanimozhi and Madras High Court Judge Justice N. Anand Venkatesh attended the event, where senior advocate Ramani Natarajan received the first copy. Speaking at the function, Ms. Kanimozhi said the book documented how an atheist movement and Periyar, who held atheistic principles as a primary philosophy of his life, played a leading role in temple entry struggles. She emphasised that the Dravidian movement, despite seeking to break down a religion that protects caste, fought relentlessly and won, to guarantee that believers faced no restrictions when entering temples. “If we are fighting today to ensure that fields like medicine, the judiciary, IT, and industry become inclusive spaces for everyone, the entry into temples served as the very starting point for all these struggles, a fact Manu articulates clearly,” Ms. Kanimozhi added. Justice Anand Venkatesh pointed to the book’s record of a board near the Mahadeva Temple in the Travancore Princely State, which specified with mathematical precision how far each caste should stand from a Namboodiri priest and remarked: “When viewing these rules, the heart of anyone with human empathy will tremble.” He further noted, “The historical court procedure for recording testimony from members of oppressed communities truly shook me.” He affirmed that the right to worship was not a religious privilege, but a fundamental right of a citizen, adding that individual autonomy and dignity took precedence over ancient societal beliefs. Participating in the discussion later, Mr. Manuraj said: “Even after 100 years, we have not achieved complete equality in temples. We still have many more steps to take on this journey. Therefore, the purpose of this book is to describe how this struggle has continued.” He expressed optimism for the future, saying, “Through this book, you will read how society has progressed over 100 years of legal struggles—moving from a state where people could not even walk on the streets near temples to today’s debates surrounding the appointment of temple priests. While this transformation took 100 years, I hope it will not take another 100 years to appoint women or transgender persons as priests.” Published - August 09, 2026 12:22 am IST Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. national_raw_news.title: Bid to ‘silence’ him for investigative journalism: Tejpal’s daughter on his conviction in rape case
national_raw_news.content: Updated - August 09, 2026 12:49 pm IST - Panaji A file image of Tarun Tejpal. | Photo Credit: Atish Pomburfekar Former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal’s daughter Cara Tejpal has linked his conviction by the Bombay High Court to his investigative journalism, claiming he was targeted because of the magazine's work and the rape allegation was used as a means to “silence” him. In a statement issued on Saturday (August 8, 2026), Ms. Cara Tejpal said she did not care if she was labelled a “rape apologist” or the “child of a rapist”. Also read: Tarun Tejpal case - a timeline She sought to link the case to Tehelka’s investigative journalism and the "controversies surrounding the magazine’s reports on corruption" and alleged wrongdoing by those in power. “Tarun Tejpal was more than a thorn in the side of the BJP government, and what better way to silence him than to portray him as the most reviled of all sinners—a rapist,” the statement said. The HC on Thursday (August 6, 2026) convicted the 62-year-old journalist of raping a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in 2013 during an event organised by the magazine in Goa. The verdict came on an appeal filed by the Goa government against his acquittal. Ms. Cara Tejpal said she had examined the evidence in the case for 13 years and was convinced that her father was innocent. “I was 23 years old when my father was arrested. I was 31 when he was acquitted, and today, at 36, I stand by him as he is convicted by the Bombay High Court on the basis of a false allegation of rape filed suo moto by the state of Goa,” she said. Ms. Cara Tejpal said she had initially been “terrified of speaking the truth” when her father was arrested and was deeply affected by the media coverage surrounding the case. She said she was no longer willing to remain silent despite the criticism she could face for supporting her father. “I’m not that 23-year-old anymore. I’m 36, and I couldn’t care less about being called a ‘rape apologist’ or ‘child of rapist’ or whatever vile slur is used against me,” she said. She further alleged that the case was accompanied by a strong public narrative that discouraged people from questioning the allegations. “The truth is the truth. No court, no Prime Minister, no godi media can take that from us,” she said, urging people to read the “actual facts of the case” rather than relying on headlines and what she described as uninformed public discourse. Tarun Tejpal was arrested in November 2013 following allegations that he had sexually assaulted a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator during an event organised by the Tehelka magazine in Goa. The sessions court at Mapusa acquitted him in May 2021, prompting the Goa government to challenge it before the HC. The High Court termed the trial court’s verdict as “perverse”, noting that it fell for the notion that a sexual assault complainant must be a “perfect victim” and conduct herself in a certain way so as to appear credible. The court asked Tarun Tejpal to surrender within two weeks, but later extended the period to four weeks on a request from his lawyers. The journalist has claimed that he was a political victim and would approach the Supreme Court to challenge his conviction. national_raw_news.title: Jharkhand students protest LIVE updates: Fasting students decline hospitalisation; say govt. 'playing games'
national_raw_news.content: Updated - August 09, 2026 12:25 pm IST Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto during his indefinite hunger strike as part of a protest against the Jharkhand government over alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC examination, JSSC-CGL and other recruitment tests, demanding a CBI probe and reforms in the recruitment agencies, at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, in Ranchi, Jharkhand. File. | Photo Credit: PTI A s the first five rounds of talks failed to break the deadlock, the Jharkhand government has decided to hold a sixth round of talks with student representatives around 12 noon on Sunday (August 9, 2026). A series of meetings with student groups throughout Saturday (August 8, 2026) culminated in the Jharkhand government announcing fresh talks with aspirants protesting against alleged irregularities in recruitment exams in the State that prompted a prominent students’ faction accusing it of “political manoeuvring”. Also read | Years of delayed exams, bribery allegations provoke Jharkhand protests As the protest entered its 15th day on Saturday (August 8, 2026), the Hemant Soren government held four rounds of talks with different student groups, including the Congress’ student wing NSUI, Jharkhand Chhatra Manch and Adivasi Chhatra Sangh. The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch accused the Jharkhand government of “political manoeuvring” by announcing another round of talks with student organisations, alleging the move was aimed at creating divisions among protesting students and diverting people’s attention from their core demands. Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) MLA Jairam Mahto sat on a one-day fast in Ranchi on Sunday (August 9) to support students protesting over irregularities in examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).- ANI On July 23, students began gathering at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi. They arrived carrying bedding, notebooks and plastic folders filled with admit cards from examinations that, in many cases, had defined nearly a decade of their lives. Their demand was straightforward: cancel all examinations tainted by allegations of corruption, order an independent investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), and overhaul the state’s recruitment system. JD(U) National Spokesperson Rajeev Ranjan Prasad on Sunday (August 9) said the ongoing protest by JPSC-JSSC aspirants in Ranchi has transformed into a mass movement, alleging growing resentment among students and young people over the conduct of competitive examinations and recruitment in Jharkhand.- ANI As the intense protests by JPSC-JSSC aspirants continue at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi, a doctors team inspected the health of protestors on Sunday (August 9). Speaking to ANI , Dr. AP Sinha assured that the fasting students have declined hospitalisation despite experiencing a drop in body weight. However, they remain alert, stable, and fine for now.- ANI A team of doctors from the Sadar Hospital, Ranchi, inspected the health of JPSC-JSSC aspirants staging a hunger strike at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.- ANI Amid ongoing protests over irregularities in Jharkhand’s recruitment examinations, student leader Ravindra Paswan accused the State government of attempting to fragment the movement and warned of a massive ‘Vidhan Sabha Gherao’ march on August 10 if demands were not met. “What we have witnessed from the government’s side today has left us very upset. Look at the game the government is playing: today, they accepted memoranda from about 6-7 other organisations. Why are they doing this? What is their intention?” he said. Questioning the State government’s decision to receive a memorandum from the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI), the Congress’ student wing, Mr. Paswan added, “Why are they taking memoranda from NSUI? NSUI is the Congress student wing. What kind of demands would they make? Why are they not on the street protesting against the government?” “The government is playing games, trying to fragment this movement into 2-3 different factions,” he alleged.- ANI On talks with govt. student protestor Prem Nayak said, “We were called today at 12 noon by the government. But the government wants to give us toffees and biscuits to coax us like children... We demand that the Chief Minister talk to us directly and take strict action. What issue does he have with that?... Let’s see what happens today after the team goes for the meet.”- ANI The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, a prominent students’ group spearheading the protest in Jharkhand against alleged exam irregularities, accused the state government of “political manoeuvring” by announcing it would hold another round of talks with the demonstrators. The group alleged that despite placing all points before the government during a meeting on Friday night, the panel chose to call Congress and JMM-affiliated students’ bodies who had no role in the agitation and took their charter of demands on Saturday. “This is political manoeuvring by the government. It is trying to create a divide among students and divert people’s attention. But, they should know all students are united,” said Ravindra Paswan, a leader of JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch. As rain continued to fall over Ranchi on Saturday (August 8, 2026), the students’ protest at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium entered its 15th day with no sign of retreat. A seven-member delegation of the Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) met the government committee, carrying with it the demands that have kept hundreds of aspirants on the streets since July 25, with no immediate breakthrough in sight. Jharkhand protests enter 15th day as government invites JLKM leaders for talks amid demands for exam irregularity investigations. national_raw_news.title: Farmers association welcomes Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s move on linking Godavari-Cauvery-Gundar rivers
national_raw_news.content: Published - August 09, 2026 12:22 pm IST - VIRUDHUNAGAR Southern Districts Farmers Association has welcomed the move of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, who has appealed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for execution of Godavari-Cauvery-Gundar river linking project in totality. The association functionary, R. Ram Pandian, recalled the Chief Minister’s communication to Prime Minister seeking to instruct the Union Ministry of Jal Jeevan on this issue. The National Water Development Agency has planned to execute the project linking Godavari, Pennar, Palar and Vellar. This project would benefit only some parts of the northern districts of Tamil Nadu as the project would terminate few km ahead of Cauvery river. It would not fulfill the water needs of southern districts. The Chief Minister has insisted that the project should be implemented as per its earlier plan of interlining Cauvery, Vaigai and Gundar to benefit the Gundar basin irrigation systems. Mr. Pandian said only then lakhs of acres of ayacut in the districts of Pudukottai, Ramanathapuram, Sivaganga, Virudhunagar and Thoothukudi would get permanent water source for irrigation. “Otherwise, the water source for these districts will become out of reach for farmers. That the Chief Minister has urged the Prime Minister that the full benefit of the scheme should reach the farmers of Tamil Nadu is very heartening for the farmers,” he added. In the present situation, these districts are facing severe drought-like situation. With reduced water source, it affects irrigation and people are also facing drinking water shortage. Similarly, the farmers’ livelihood is affected due to water shortage for cattle,” Mr. Pandian said. Making use of the 1,100 TMC of water of Godavari basin that is draining wastefully into the sea would help fulfil water needs of Telangana, Andhra, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Pudhucherry, he added. The water source of 18 minor rivers flowing in Pudukottai, Sivaganga and Ramanathapuram and the seven distributaries of Gundar river flowing from Madurai would get augmented providing ample drinking water for over lakhs of people. It would also help to increase the coverage of cultivation, Mr. Pandian said. The association urged the Centre to consider this demand of Tamil Nadu and execute it in totality to improve the surface water source in the State. national_raw_news.title: Bengal Government hospitals observe two-minute silence in memory of R.G. Kar rape-murder victim doctor
national_raw_news.content: Published - August 09, 2026 12:20 pm IST - Kolkata A two-minute silence was observed by doctors, nurses and other officials at all government hospitals in memory of the doctor. Representational file image. | Photo Credit: AP A two-minute silence was observed on Sunday (August 9, 2026) in all government hospitals across West Bengal in memory of the on-duty doctor who was raped and murdered at R .G. Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata on the second anniversary of her death. The West Bengal Junior Doctors' Front, which led extensive protests following the discovery of the post-graduate trainee doctor's body on August 9, 2024, held a clinic for underprivileged people at Chitpur in north Kolkata. "We are holding the clinic seeking justice for the on-duty doctor who was raped and murdered," said one participating doctor. A two-minute silence was observed by doctors, nurses and other officials at all government hospitals in memory of the doctor. State's Health and Family Welfare Minister Dr Sharadwat Mukherjee and senior officials observed a two-minute silence at Swasthya Bhavan, the department's headquarters, in Salt Lake. At R.G. Kar Medical College and Hospital here in north Kolkata, paramilitary personnel guarding the facility joined the doctors, nurses, and other staff in observing the silence. Following the gruesome rape and murder of the on-duty doctor, the Supreme Court had ordered a slew of measures to ensure safety and security of doctors and other staff, including deployment of paramilitary personnel at R.G. Kar Medical College and Hospital. While one Sanjay Roy was convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment till the end of his life by the Sealdah sessions court, the victim doctor's parents and many of her colleagues have been claiming that other people were also involved in the crime. The CBI is holding an investigation into the alleged conspiracy angle in the rape and murder of the post-graduate trainee doctor on an order of the Calcutta High Court. The victim doctor's mother was elected to the West Bengal Assembly as a BJP candidate from Panihati in North 24 Parganas district in the April elections. national_raw_news.title: P.M. Bhargava: The Indian man who saw tomorrow in a cell
national_raw_news.content: Updated - August 09, 2026 12:19 pm IST - HYDERABAD The book cover of ‘The Man and The Making of Modern Biology in India’. | Photo Credit: arranged The double-helix structure of DNA was postulated in 1953. By 1959, Pushpa M. Bhargava, a chemistry PhD who switched to biology, wrote a note to create a Biological Laboratory of India. By 1977, Hyderabad had the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology carved out of the space of the IICT. A new biography by Bhargava’s long-time associate Chandana Chakrabarti ‘The Man and The Making of Modern Biology in India’ brings to life the fascinating story of India’s modern biology, its tryst with irrationality, homoeopathy, fish ‘prasadam’, bureaucracy and the man who saw tomorrow in a cell. Edited excerpts from an interview with The Hindu ’s Serish Nanisetti. Chandana Chakrabarti | Photo Credit: MOHAMMED YOUSUF The Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology and Pushpa M. Bhargava are synonymous even after decades, what’s the origin story? Dr. Bhargava or as everyone called him PMB did his schooling in Uttar Pradesh, and PhD in chemistry at Lucknow University. He was homeschooled until Class IX, as schools considered him too advanced for his age. After PhD he knew the future belonged to biology at cellular level and switched to that field and trained himself for it. While writing the book, I discovered the 1959 note that he had typed out for an institute of biology and CCMB was an exact match of that vision decades later. Q: How did Bhargava come to Hyderabad? Hussain Zaheer of Central Laboratories for Scientific and Industrial Research (CLSIR which became Regional Research Laboratory) knew him from Lucknow and invited him after his PhD. Although Lucknow University offered him a job, he felt it had limited prospects and chose Hyderabad instead. He first worked as a lecturer at Mahabub College, then joined the Chemistry Department at Osmania University, before Mr. Zaheer found him a position at CLSRI. He lived at Zeenat Mahal, Tarnaka, sharing a house with scholars, including Abdul Rahman and K.T. Achaya. Why did he want to leave chemistry? He grew restless doing chemistry at Osmania, feeling it wouldn’t take him far, and became convinced biology was the field with a future. He decided the only way to make the shift was to go abroad. He got a post-doc with Charles Heidelberger at the University of Wisconsin, working on a molecule still used in cancer treatment. There he encountered the excitement around Francis Crick’s DNA work, met his future wife Manorama, and developed his political views during the McCarthy era. He then did a second post-doc at the National Institute for Medical Research (NIMR), Mill Hill, UK, where his actual transition from chemistry to biology took place, largely self-taught. How did the idea for a national biological laboratory begin? Bhargava drafted a note in 1959 proposing a national biological laboratory, arguing India was missing the molecular biology revolution. The proposal was repeatedly rejected by committees, as traditional chemists and biologists opposed it. He organised an international seminar on modern biology at Regional Research Laboratory to demonstrate the field’s importance and kept resubmitting the note, including again in 1964. What triggered the eventual approval? The 1973 oil crisis prompted him to write directly to Dr. Nayudamma, the new CSIR Director-General, warning that India could not afford to fall behind in biotechnology (ethanol as a biofuel took off in 70s led by Brazil). This led to a committee, and on April 1, 1977, CCMB was formed on paper, evolving from the Department of Biochemistry. A lab is not a building but people and scientists? Rather than judging candidates only on academic knowledge, he tested their powers of observation and their willingness to disagree with him, even when he stated something incorrect with authority. He recruited talent such as Lalji Singh, who worked on sex determination in organisms, including temperature-dependent determination in crocodiles. There was no hierarchy in CCMB. Everyone addressed each other by first name, including him, that set it apart from other institutions. There was a shared-resource system where grant money went into a common pool rather than individual labs duplicating equipment. How was the building finally inaugurated? Bhargava avoided foundation-stone ceremonies, insisting a laboratory be dedicated only once fully functional. He invited Rajiv Gandhi two years in advance to dedicate CCMB, fixing the date for November 26, 1987, even though construction was far from complete at the time of the invitation. Is CCMB his only contribution to Indian science? No. He set up the Guha Research Conference, which grew out of dissatisfaction with the Indian Science Congress and became a leading forum for molecular biologists. He also wrote a science textbook for children for NCERT. And he created a massive exhibition on the scientific method, which was dismantled during the Morarji Desai government. His contribution to science and rationality was not limited to labs. He famously took on the case of ‘fish cure' teaming up with Jana Vignana Vedika demanding that it cannot be called medicine. Now it is called fish prasadam. He made a case before a national panel for ‘ban on cow slaughter in 1966’ that had RSS chief M.S. Golwalkar as its member along with Shankaracharyas (the committee never submitted the report). He opposed government funding for homeopathy, and challenged attempts to introduce astrology as a university science course, taking the case to the Andhra Pradesh High Court and Supreme Court. How did the biography of Bhargava come to be written? I obtained his diaries dating back to 1948 and recorded extended interviews with him. including a long stretch of them in Deauville in France. The manuscript was completed and shown to him in 2016; he approved it before his death in 2017. Then COVID-19 intervened and finally now it has been published. national_raw_news.title: Two men held for taking photographs inside Arunachaleswarar temple
national_raw_news.content: Updated - August 09, 2026 12:09 pm IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI The photographs of the sanctum sanctorum were taken with a micro camera fitted to a spectacle. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Two men from Telangana were held for taking photographs of the sanctum sanctorum using a micro camera-fitted spectacle inside Arunachaleswarar temple in Tiruvannamalai town on Saturday. The incident occured in the wake of the visit of Union Home Minister Amit Shah to the temple town to offer prayers at the temple in the evening. The police said the identified persons were Mounish, 27, a software professional, and his friend Magesh. Both of them are residents of Hyderabad in Telangana. The police said that they were waiting in queue to offer prayers at the temple when light flashed from the spectacle of Mounish. Other devotees who saw the flash alerted temple staff, who in turn, informed senior officials of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department. The police said signages were installed to warn devotees against taking photographs and videos inside the temple. Based on a complaint by temple staff, the Tiruvannamalai Town police have detained the duo. A probe is under way. national_raw_news.title: Former Chief Justice of Manipur High Court D. Krishnakumar appointed Chairman of T.N. Law Commission
national_raw_news.content: Published - August 09, 2026 12:06 pm IST - CHENNAI Former Chief Justice of Manipur High Court D. Krishnakumar. File | Photo Credit: M. Govarthan The Tamil Nadu government has reconstituted the State Law Commission and appointed Justice D. Krishnakumar, former Chief Justice of the Manipur High Court, as its Chairman. A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Law Department. Justice R.M.T. Teekaa Raman, former judge of the Madras High Court; T.K. Ramachandran, former Additional Chief Secretary; and A. Arunagiri, former Secretary, Law Department, have been appointed as full-time members. P. Mohan Doss and R. Govindarajan, both former District Judges, have been appointed as part-time members. An officer in the cadre of Secretary, Law Department, will be the full-time Member Secretary. The term of office of the Chairman, full-time members and part-time members will be three years from the date of assumption of charge by the Chairman. national_raw_news.title: Veerashaiva-Lingayat institutions played key role in promoting education in North Karnataka: M.B. Patil
national_raw_news.content: Updated - August 09, 2026 11:54 am IST - KALABURAGI Minister for Large and Medium Industries M.B. Patil speaking during the inauguration the two-day centenary celebrations of Heerada Sugamma School in Ballari on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Veerashaiva-Lingayat organisations and educational institutions played a significant role in providing education to people in North Karnataka even before Independence period, Minister for Large and Medium Industries M.B. Patil said on Saturday. He was speaking after inaugurating the two-day centenary celebrations of Heerada Sugamma School, the first school established by the Veerashaiva Vidyavardhaka Sangha, on the school premises in Ballari. Mr. Patil said institutions established by Veerashaiva-Lingayat organisations had contributed substantially to the spread of education in the region. Referring to educational institutions run by Siddaganga Mutt and Gavisiddeshwara Mutt in Koppal, he said such institutions had provided education to thousands of children without restricting their services to members of any particular community. He said the institutions had been sustained and developed over the years through the contributions of several individuals and stressed the need to preserve cultural traditions while embracing modernity. “Artificial intelligence and robotics are making a significant impact across sectors, and we need to pay attention to these emerging fields. With foreign universities entering the country, our educational institutions must provide education that enables students to compete with them,” he said. Mr. Patil also called for the contributions made by donors towards the development of educational institutions to be utilised efficiently and effectively. He expressed the hope that such institutions would continue to contribute to the development of society. The seer of Mahanta Mutt, Emmiganur, said Veerashaiva Mutts had contributed to society not merely through religious institutions but by establishing educational institutions and spreading knowledge. The community’s tradition of anna dasoha and akshara dasoha had contributed to the creation of an egalitarian society, he said, recalling the message of Basavanna that all people should live in happiness. The Mutts had played an important role in spreading the light of knowledge, he added. Legislative Council member Shashil G. Namoshi released a souvenir brought out to mark the centenary celebrations. Recalling the efforts made to establish educational institutions in the Kalyana Karnataka region, Mr. Patil said the then Chief Minister S. Nijalingappa had facilitated the collection of a 2.5% cess from farmers for the purpose. He called for the simplification of government rules for establishing colleges and stressed the need to ensure quality education. Minister B. Nagendra launched the foundation work for installing stone statues of the seers of Hanagal and Ujjaini and of Heerada Sugamma. He said both he and his father had studied in colleges run by the Veerashaiva Vidyavardhaka Sangha. Ballari MP E. Tukaram laid the foundation for free hostels proposed to be established by the Veerashaiva Vidyavardhaka Sangha. Describing Heerada Sugamma as an “Akshara Avva”, he said education, he urged people to contribute to the development of educational institutions and work for social progress while upholding the Constitution throughout their lives. Former Minister Allam Veerabhadrappa, sangha president K. Kanekal Mahantesh, seers of Palthur, All-India Veerashaiva Lingayat Mahasabha women’s wing national president Veena Kashappanavar, Mayor P. Gaddeppa, Lidkar chairman Mundrigi Nagaraj, school management committee president and sangha joint secretary Meti Yalpi Pampanagouda, sangha vice-president Janekunte Basavaraj, executive committee members and senior auditor Sirigeri Pannaraj were among those present.
